notes: TBox rule edit: the material of the ziggurat (a sun-dried mud-brick core, usually faced with baked brick) is swapped for cut stone, the material of the Egyptian pyramids it is often compared with, plausible and clearly false. Derivability very_unlikely: stated directly in every description of the type. No real exceptions: every Mesopotamian and Elamite ziggurat had a mud-brick core; an Assyrian stone revetment on a lower stage (Nimrud) leaves the body brick. Relation built_from. The three derived queries name the ziggurat of Nippur, the larger temple tower on Tell Ingharra at Kish and the temple tower at Aqar Quf (Dur-Kurigalzu) as ziggurats in the prompt; the Nippur prompt is plain. The famous members (Chogha Zanbil, Etemenanki) are not asked. The cross-lingual questions are choices (brick or cut stone). The near query (Ur-Nammu) differs from the new answer and is no premise. Caveat: Aqar Quf's mud-brick and reed-mat construction is described in Wikipedia's Dur-Kurigalzu article (86 of 435 pages co-occur), so its material may be stored by name.
